nodes.name: Learner's licence
nodes.description: The first licence. You apply online on Sarathi, visit the RTO with the printed application, and pass the learner's licence test.

metadata.whyRequired: You cannot apply for a permanent driving licence without holding a learner's licence for the same class of vehicle first.
metadata.whatToDo: Apply online on Sarathi under New Learner's Licence, print the filled application with its reference number, then submit it at your chosen RTO office.
metadata.expectedOutput: A learner's licence, valid across India for 6 months.
metadata.fee: Rs. 150.00 to issue the licence in Form 3, plus Rs. 50.00 test fee

sources.evidence: Applicants can visit https://sarathi.parivahan.gov.in/sarathiservice and apply for Learner Licence ONLINE by following the link “New Learning Licence“ Applicants should take print of the duly filled-in ONLINE application along with the reference number and submit at the chosen RTO office.
FORM 2 [Refer Rules 10, 14, 17 and 18] FORM OF APPLICATION FOR LEARNER’S LICENCE OR DRIVING LICENCE OR ADDITION OF A NEW CLASS OF VEHICLE OR RENEWAL OF DRIVING LICENCE OR CHANGE OF ADDRESS OR NAME

nodes.name: Driving licence
nodes.description: The permanent licence. Applied for in Form 4 along with the learner's licence, and granted after you pass the test of competence to drive.

metadata.whyRequired: No person shall drive a motor vehicle in any public place unless he holds an effective driving licence issued to him by the Licensing Authority.
metadata.whatToDo: Apply in Form 4 along with your learner's licence, book the test of competence, and bring a vehicle of the class you are applying for.
metadata.expectedOutput: A driving licence, sent by speed post to the address you gave.
metadata.fee: Rs. 200.00 to issue the driving licence
metadata.timeline: Sent by speed post after you pass the test of competence

sources.evidence: No person shall drive a motor vehicle in any public place unless he holds an effective driving licence issued to him by the Licensing Authority, authorising him to drive the vehicle.
An application in Form 4, for a permanent driving licence shall be made along with the Learners' Licence obtained for such class of vehicle.
The candidate who passes the test of competence successfully will be issued with a driving licence and sent through speed post to the address furnished.

nodes.name: You must be at least 18
nodes.description: The applicant who has completed the age of eighteen years of age is eligible to apply for a driving licence to drive a motor vehicle other than a transport vehicle.

sources.evidence: The applicant who has completed the age of eighteen years of age is eligible to apply for a driving licence to drive a motor vehicle other than a transport vehicle.

sources.evidence: An applicant who has completed twenty years of age will be eligible for applying for a licence to drive a transport vehicle.

nodes.name: Parent or guardian declaration
nodes.officialName: Declaration under sub-section (2) of section 7 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
nodes.description: Signed by the person who has care of a minor applicant, accepting responsibility for their driving. It is printed on Form 2 itself.

metadata.whatToDo: Have the parent or guardian fill and sign the declaration section of Form 2 giving consent for the learner's licence.

sources.evidence:
Under sub-section (2) of section 7 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988

Shri/Smt./Kumari ......................................... son/daughter ........................................
of .................................... who is a minor is under my care and I accept responsibility for
his/her driving. If at a later date I decide not to accept responsibility for his/her driving,
I shall inform the licensing authority in writing for the cancellation of the licence. I give
my consent for his/her obtaining the learner's licence.

nodes.name: Learner's licence
nodes.description: Valid throughout India for 6 months. If it expires you start the whole process again.

sources.evidence: The Learner Licence is valid through out India for a period of 6 months only. In case of expiry of the Learner Licence the applicant needs to repeat the process afresh.

nodes.name: Visit the RTO for document verification and biometrics
nodes.description: Online is only half of it. The application goes under scrutiny, which means physically showing up at the RTO.

metadata.whyRequired: Scrutiny means applicant has to visit the concerned RTO for physical verification of documents and submit Biometrics to complete the process.
metadata.whatToDo: Carry four printed things: the acknowledgement that lists your required documents, the application form with Form 1 and Form 1A, the appointment letter, and the fee receipt. Take the original documents too, not just the uploads.

sources.evidence: Scrutiny means applicant has to visit the concerned RTO for physical verification of documents and submit Biometrics to complete the process.

After completing online procedure, for further processing of application you should visit the concerned RTO office with the required documents as shown on the acknowledgtement slip. You should also carry a copy of the fee receipt.

1. Check the application status and click on print acknowledgment which shows required documents.

2. Click on print Form 1 & can download application form & Form 1A

3. Click on Appointment letter from the same application status.

4. Fee receipt.

nodes.name: Pass the learner's licence test
nodes.description: A computer test on traffic rules and signs. It is an online test, but you sit it at the RTO, not at home.

metadata.whyRequired: You do not get a learner's licence without passing it.
metadata.whatToDo: Report to the RTO you applied to, or to its authorised learning licence test centre, on your appointment date.
metadata.expectedOutput: A pass, after which the learner's licence is issued.
metadata.fee: Rs. 50.00 test fee or repeat test fee

sources.evidence:
Yes, you have to pass the online test (STALL Test) to get Learner's License. After the completion of its one

month you need to appear for driving test to get your driving license.
You need to report the concerned RTO or their authorized learning license test center.
Learner’s licence test fee or repeat test fee, as the case may be | Rs. 50.00/-

nodes.name: Book a slot for the driving test

metadata.whatToDo: Schedule the test of competence online, or at an RTO office where that facility exists. Where neither is available, schedule directly at the office concerned.
metadata.expectedOutput: An appointment for the test of competence.

sources.evidence: Schedule an appointment for the test of competence online by visiting the website or any RTO office where such facility exists. In other cases schedule an appointment directly at the Office Concerned.

nodes.name: Pass the test of competence to drive

metadata.whyRequired: The driving licence is only granted after this test is passed.
metadata.whatToDo: Bring a vehicle of the type your application is for. You must satisfy the officer of your ability to perform the tasks in Rule 15(2) of the CMVR.
metadata.expectedOutput: A pass, after which the licence is issued and posted.
metadata.fee: Rs. 300.00 for the test or repeat test, for each class of vehicle

sources.evidence: The applicant should bring a vehicle of the type to which the application relates.
The applicant should satisfy the officer conducting the test regarding his capability to drive the vehicle and his ability to perform the tasks specified in Rule-15(2) of the CMVR.
